units.title: Pronunciation, Vowel Sounds
units.intro: Pronunciation: vowel sounds and silent letters.

cards.title: Pronunciation: vowel sounds and silent letters
rule: English spelling and sound do not always match: *ough* sounds different in *cough, through, though, enough*.

**Silent letters:** *b* after *m* (*climb, thumb, comb*) and in *debt, doubt*; *k* before *n* (*know, knife*); *w* before *r* (*write, wrong*); *h* in *hour, honest*; *t* in *listen, castle*; *g* before *n* (*sign, foreign*).
**Short and long vowels:** *ship /ɪ/ – sheep /iː/, full /ʊ/ – fool /uː/, cat /æ/ – cart /ɑː/*. Changing the vowel can change the word.
The **-ed** ending has three sounds: /t/ after voiceless sounds (*walked, watched*), /d/ after voiced sounds (*played, lived*), /ɪd/ after t or d (*wanted, needed*).

examples.fix: "Hour" begins with a vowel sound: an hour.

cards.pattern: silent: mb · kn · wr · (h)our · lis(t)en · si(g)n

cards.title: Notes
body: **Exam method:** say each word quietly and listen for the odd one out.
Use *an* before a vowel **sound**: *an hour, an honest man*, but *a university, a European*.

cards.problem: Choose the word in which the underlined letter is voiced (NOT silent):

steps.text: **Step 1: Look at the sentence.** English spelling rules dictate that 'b' is silent after 'm' at the end of a word (*climb, thumb*) or before 't' (*debt*).
In 'timber', 'b' is in the middle of a syllable and is fully voiced (/ˈtɪmbər/).

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Choose the word in which the underlined letter is voiced (NOT silent):
cards.why:
**Step 1: Look at the sentence**
Silent 'h' occurs in words of French origin such as 'honest', 'hour', and 'honor'. In 'house', 'h' is a fully voiced glottal fricative (/haʊs/).

**Step 2: Watch out for the trap**
Students often fail to identify French silent 'h' words, pronouncing the 'h' in 'honest'. Option D is correct because 'h' is voiced.

**Step 3: In Tigrinya**
'H' ኣብ ላቲን/ፈረንሳይ መበቆል ዘለዎም ቃላት (honest, hour, honor) ዘይድመጽ ይኸውን። ኣብ 'house' (ገዛ) ግን እቲ 'h' ከም 'ሆ' ብንጹር ይድመጽ። ስለዚ ቅኑዕ መልሲ Option D እዩ።

cards.title: Worked practice
cards.problem: Identify the word that contains an 'Odd' pronunciation of the underlined letters:

steps.text: **Step 1: Look at the sentence.** The 'ch' digraph has different pronunciations based on word origin.
In 'chemistry', 'character', and 'chaos', 'ch' is pronounced as `/k/` (Greek origin).
In 'machine', it is pronounced as `/ʃ/` (French origin).

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Identify the word that contains an 'Odd' pronunciation of the underlined letters:
cards.why:
**Step 1: Look at the sentence**
In 'chef', 'machine', and 'brochure', the 'ch' is pronounced as `/ʃ/` (French origin). In 'choir', it is pronounced as `/k/` followed by a glide (/kwaɪər/).

**Step 2: Watch out for the trap**
Students often mispronounce 'choir' as /tʃɔɪər/ due to spelling. Option D is the odd one because it is pronounced as `/k/`.

**Step 3: In Tigrinya**
'Chef', 'machine',ን 'brochure'ን ናይ ፈረንሳይ መበቆል ስለ ዘለዎም እቲ 'ch' ከም 'ሾ' (/ʃ/) ይድመጽ። 'Choir' (መዘምራን) ግን ክንብብ ከለና 'ኳየር' (/kwaɪər/) ስለ ዝበሃል ፍሉይ ኣደማምጻ ኣለዎ (Option D)።

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Which word has the same vowel sound as "book"?
cards.why:
**Step 1:** "book" has the short /ʊ/ sound.

**Step 2:** "could" /kʊd/ has the same sound.

**Step 3:** "boot" /uː/, "blood" /ʌ/ and "boat" /əʊ/ are different.

**Tip:** Say each word aloud slowly and compare the vowel sound, not the spelling. The same letters can have different sounds (bread / bead).
